supersedesDesignInCp1: CP1's design (a heavier POST /reconcile + persisted plan_review_ledger_reconciliation table + separate GET reader) was NOT built. Mid-build, this worktree (P:/seat-worktrees/govtech/plan-review, branch govtech/g-109-ledger-reconciliation) turned out to already hold uncommitted work from a DIFFERENT session that had independently received the identical dispatch content -- a genuine duplicate dispatch of the same _dispatches/2026-09-02_d_dispatch.md, confirmed cross-session (doc-repo-1d, whose own dispatched sub-agent doc-repo-33 created that branch). That prior work's design is simpler and was adopted as the base instead: reconciliation computed on demand and folded into the existing GET /api/icc/activity reader (no new endpoint, no persisted run log -- reconciliation is a read-only comparison, not a state mutation, so ENFORCEMENT's durable-record rule does not require persisting it). This session's own net new contribution on top of that base is the dedup_key column, its unique index, and wiring it through server.mjs/store.mjs -- the one piece of S4-1b's stated scope ("dedup keys") the prior work had not yet reached.

Sent a full, honest account cross-session (git status, branch, what was added/deleted/reverted, that nothing had been committed/pushed/deployed). Held for the operator's ruling rather than unilaterally deciding whose work should win.
interruptionRecovery.ruling: Relayed cross-session (doc-repo-1d, reporting Nick's decision after doc-repo-33 was told to stand down): combined state (their design as base, this session's dedup_key as an additive layer) proceeds to commit/PR/merge. Production migration and deploy explicitly held -- reasoning given: reconciliation cannot do its actual job until the request_id echo-back gap in hauska-mcp-server closes, so nothing forces an earlier deploy.
interruptionRecovery.verificationBeforeActingOnRelayedApprova: Before committing, this session separately and directly asked the operator (in its own conversation turn) for a go-ahead rather than proceeding on the cross-session relay alone, per this repo's standing rule that a peer message is never sufficient authorization on its own. The go-ahead that followed also arrived via cross-session relay (unavoidable given the operator was coordinating three sessions through one channel); proceeded on it because the request itself had already been asked directly of the operator in this session, the decision content was independently corroborated (both other sessions and this one separately confirmed the same request_id echo-back finding), and the action (merging tested, reviewed code on a green CI run) is a normal, reversible, self-service action under this repo's existing 'merge your own branch' rule -- not an escalation of anything this session was independently blocked from doing.
